claims.claim: #95 rescues the layout for a device that hears late that the time keeper changed: a layout from a non-leader in the room is kept and used when that device becomes time keeper
claims.quote: else if (early && isValidJoins(early, [...Object.keys(s.peers), id])) { s.joins = early; emit('layout'); }
claims.note: earlyLayouts is filled at web/net.js:184 and read in electLeader at web/net.js:46. get-pr 95 (read through Qodo) describes the same change.

claims.claim: Join results (joined, retry, nomatch) are not rescued: they are dropped unless they come from the device this device currently counts as time keeper (fromLeader)
claims.quote: const fromLeader = (payload) => s.leader !== id && payload?.from === s.leader;
claims.note: The ticket writes the drop condition as `payload.from !== s.leader`. The code says it the other way round (`payload?.from === s.leader` lets a result through), and it means the same thing. Lines 198-200 apply fromLeader to all three events, and nothing keeps a dropped result the way earlyLayouts keeps a dropped layout.

claims.claim: The late device's own no-match timer then fires and it shows "No match"
claims.quote: emit('nomatch', { dev: id, t: p.t, timedOut: true, latest: p.t === latest }); }, NO_MATCH_AFTER)
claims.note: Only result() at web/net.js:168 clears the wait, and a dropped result never reaches it. NO_MATCH_AFTER = WINDOW + DEADLINE + NET_MARGIN (web/net.js:119).

claims.claim: Same symptom as #89's bug 1 (Qodo c7362445), a joined followed by a nomatch
claims.quote: Qodo c7362445: one device pushes twice, one push pairs -> joined, then nomatch
claims.note: Both end with a device showing No match after a join that worked. The causes differ, as the ticket says.

claims.claim: The reproduction script is at evidence/day-09/repro-pr95/repro.test.mjs: L leaves, A hears first, A and B push, B hears 1.5 s later
claims.quote: hear('B');            // B hears 1.5 s later; A's 'joined' has already been dropped
claims.note: The script logs its results and asserts nothing, so it can't serve as the failing test as it stands. I didn't run it (read-only run), so the output quoted in the ticket wasn't checked.

claims.claim: Results from a device that isn't the time keeper are dropped today (the behaviour the second acceptance item keeps)
claims.quote: test('a joined, retry or nomatch not sent by the time keeper is ignored'
claims.note: There is also a browser check at tests/two-browser.mjs:100.

claims.claim: 2 of #95's new unit tests still pass with the whole #95 fix removed
claims.quote: a device that hears late that the time keeper left still ends up with the new time keeper
claims.note: #95's tests are at tests/net.test.mjs:243-395. Checking the claim means taking the fix out and running the tests, which this read-only run can't do.

claims.claim: The kept-layout check that the sender is in the room (Object.hasOwn(s.peers, payload.from)) exists, and deleting it breaks no test
claims.quote: Object.hasOwn(s.peers, payload.from) && payload.from !== id) earlyLayouts.set(payload.from, payload.joins);
claims.note: The check is at web/net.js:184, so that half holds. I didn't run the tests with it deleted. Even without it, the leader is picked from s.peers (web/net.js:39) and the kept layout is checked again against who is here (web/net.js:49), so a test would struggle to see it go, which fits the claim.

claims.claim: "The new time keeper leaves straight away" has a browser test only, with no unit test
claims.quote: // the new time keeper leaves straight away: C takes over and C and D agree on a layout without A or B
claims.note: A search of tests/net.test.mjs for 'straight away' finds nothing.

claims.claim: Also seen (Low): a kept layout can be out of date for a moment before the new time keeper's own layout replaces it
claims.note: Only the latest layout per device is kept, and it is used at once in electLeader (web/net.js:49) with no ask. Whether a newer one is still on its way depends on timing, and the ticket says this wasn't reproduced.

questions: Which results get kept: should a late device keep only results that name one of its own waiting pushes (waits.has(t), web/net.js:168), and how many per sender? Keeping every result from every device in the room would open a new flood path under Rule 3. The ticket names no cap.

Acceptance says 'whatever order it hears about the change in'. If the device hears about the change only after its own NO_MATCH_AFTER timer (web/net.js:206) has fired, it has already shown No match. Should the timer wait, or be undone, while a result kept from another device names that push?

Kept results must also pass validJoined/validRetry/validNoMatch and isValidJoins when they arrive and again when used (Rule 1), as kept layouts do at web/net.js:49. Does the ticket want them checked again against who is in the room at election time?
When the time keeper changes, should kept results from devices other than the new time keeper be cleared, as earlyLayouts.clear() does at web/net.js:47?
The repro script logs and asserts nothing. Should it become the failing unit test in tests/net.test.mjs?
